Before a message is admitted, a Copilot session can prepare plugins required by the organization, reporting progress as `session.info` and failures as `session.warning` with the `managed_plugins` type. While the current turn is still pending, `CopilotAgentSession` shows the progress message as the chat activity, which the waiting request's progress row reads (session activity does not reach it), and adds a failure as a warning-severity `ManagedPluginPreparationFailure` system notification. The root `user.message` echo, root `assistant.turn_start`, a failure, or the end or abort of that turn clears that activity; a late abort or idle from an earlier turn does not, and a failure reported for a waiting replacement turn is shown even while late events of the aborted turn are dropped. There is no structured plugin list, so the English message text is shown as is. Progress outside a pending turn, such as preparation started by custom agent selection, is only logged. A failure reported while no turn is waiting, such as after a background policy refresh, is kept and shown when the next message is admitted (its root `user.message` echo), unless that message's own preparation reports a newer failure or a `managed_plugins_complete` info arrives first. After a failure the runtime pauses automatic retries for about an hour or until the managed settings change. The local management bridge `retryManagedPlugins(provider, session, chat)` runs `rpc.plugins.retryManaged()` in that exact live chat right away and returns the per-plugin results; there is no client-level fallback, and the runtime throws when it does not prepare managed plugins for the session. The retry reports progress and failures through the same events, so the rules above apply; a retry in which no plugin failed drops a held failure. In chat, the failure warning ends with a trusted Retry link only when the client has that local bridge (`supportsManagedPluginRetry`); other hosts and clients show the plain warning. The link's command shows notification progress, then a warning that lists each failed plugin as `spec: error`, or information when the plugins are ready or deferred to the next message.

+A HydraFusion phase that renders in its own child chat (judge, critic, repair, revision) reaches `AgentSideEffects` as a synthetic `subagent_started` with `subagentKind: 'fusionPhase'`. That chat is presentation only: it opens on the phase's first attributed event and closes when the root turn goes idle, and the root turn owns the phase's model calls and cost. The turn tracker therefore keeps the phase turn only as context for tool-call and input-request telemetry; it never reports it as `agentHost.turnCompleted`, `agentHost.requestTokenUsage`, or `agentHost.turnHung`. Each phase is reported instead as one `agentHost.fusionPhaseCompleted` from the runtime's durable `assistant.fusion_phase_completed` / `assistant.fusion_phase_failed` record (tier, pattern, phase kind, model, status, duration, requests, tokens and nano-AIU). Phase nano-AIU is already included in the root turn's `billedNanoAiu`; do not add the two.

Behind the `chat.agentHost.experimental.prewarmSessions` setting, an idle provisional draft can launch its SDK session and start its MCP servers before the first send (`IAgentChats.warmChat`). `AgentHostSessionPrewarmer` (`node/agentHostSessionPrewarmer.ts`) decides when: the provider must support warming, the draft must have an active client and resolved customization enablement, and every launch folder, including additional multi-root folders, must be trusted. A missing trust configuration counts as untrusted; workspace-less drafts skip the trust check because their scratch folder has no workspace content. Ephemeral and imported drafts never warm. The experiment trigger is logged only after these gates, in both arms.
